comments.author: Anis Ayari
comments.comment: The hard part with local-model UX is usually not the chat box, it is making model limits visible without making users think about tokens, context windows, or image preprocessing. A simple “ChatGPT-like” shell can work well if it adds one thing: clear failure modes when the local model is slow, hallucinating, or missing context.

comments.author: Michael K.
comments.comment:
The highest-signal pattern I’ve seen is to make the agent produce a diff, not a summary: “what changed since yesterday, why it matters, and what to ignore.”

That turns a daily tool scan from content consumption into a small eval loop.

How are you filtering novelty vs. noise before it reaches the infographic stage? #AIAgents

comments.author: M. Adrees
comments.comment:
The part most people skip is the QA gate.

An agent without evals is just prompt automation with a nicer interface. I’d start with 10 real failure cases, define what “good” means, then let the workflow run only after it passes those consistently.
